gen_risks.description: Escalating insecurity and armed conflict may force suspension of field activities, causing project delays and loss of beneficiary reach.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and regularly update security SOPs, shift to remote delivery (radio, phone) in high‑risk zones, and pre‑position staff and resources in safer areas.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 3: Adaptation of Project Activities to Insecurity – Red/Black security risk descriptions

gen_risks.description: Procurement processes may be delayed by administrative routines and limited bidder competition in fragile regions, affecting timely implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit a qualified procurement specialist, adopt fast‑track procurement procedures in the PIM, and provide targeted training to DMP and bid committees.
gen_risks.evidence: Key Risks – procurement delays; Annex 2 Procurement Action Plan – need for qualified procurement specialist

gen_risks.description: The newly created PIU lacks experienced financial management staff and systems, increasing risk of mis‑allocation of funds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire FM specialist within three months, implement accounting software, and establish internal audit with IGF and ASCELC oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: Fiduciary – FM assessment notes absence of FM staff, procedures, and software

gen_risks.description: Cybersecurity breaches or data protection failures could compromise the Unique Social Registry and interoperable platforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage ANSSI for security risk assessment, implement encryption and access controls per CIL guidelines, and conduct regular penetration testing.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 2.2 – security procedures with ANSSI and CIL mentioned

gen_risks.description: Construction of warehouses and logistics hubs may cause water and soil pollution from solid and liquid waste.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply ESS 3 (Resource Efficiency) standards, require waste management plans in contracts, and monitor compliance through site inspections.
gen_risks.evidence: Key Risks – water and soil pollution from construction sites

gen_risks.description: Sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEA/SH) risks are substantial given the vulnerable target groups and conflict context.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an SEA/SH Action Plan, train all staff on code of conduct, and ensure the grievance mechanism can refer survivors to GBV services.
gen_risks.evidence: Key Risks – SEA/SH risk is Substantial; ESCP requires SEA/SH Action Plan

gen_risks.description: Gender‑based violence (GBV) may increase among women beneficiaries, undermining project outcomes and safety.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit a GBV specialist, integrate GBV risk assessments into all activities, and provide safe spaces and referral pathways for survivors.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal Covenants – requirement for GBV specialist in PIU

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related shocks (droughts, floods) could damage newly built warehouses and disrupt supply chains.
gen_risks.mitigation: Site warehouses in low‑flood zones, incorporate climate‑resilient design standards, and develop emergency repair protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Strategic Context – climate change undermines food security; Component 3.1 – warehouses built in high‑risk areas

gen_risks.description: Inadequate coordination among multiple ministries and partners may lead to fragmented implementation and duplication of effort.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a formal inter‑ministerial coordination committee, define clear roles in the PIM, and hold quarterly joint review meetings.
gen_risks.evidence: Section B – multiple ministries listed; Lessons Learned – need for stronger coordination

gen_risks.description: Delays in meeting pre‑conditions for disbursement (e.g., adoption of Productive Grants Manual) could stall cash flows to beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create a disbursement readiness checklist, monitor milestones weekly, and provide technical assistance to finalize manuals ahead of deadlines.
gen_risks.evidence: Disbursement Arrangements – withdrawals contingent on Productive Grants Manual adoption

gen_risks.description: Limited mobile network coverage and low phone penetration may hinder digital payments and remote monitoring.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct a telecom coverage mapping, supplement with cash points and agent networks, and retain paper‑based backup mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 2.2 – payment platform considerations include mobile network coverage

gen_risks.description: Exclusion of vulnerable groups (women, youth, persons with disabilities, IDPs) from benefits due to targeting errors.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply gender‑sensitive targeting criteria, conduct community validation workshops, and monitor inclusion indicators quarterly.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1.1 – gender‑sensitive targeting; Key Risks – exclusion of vulnerable groups

gen_risks.description: Corruption or fraud in procurement and cash transfers could erode project credibility and financial resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement strict procurement oversight via ASCELC, use e‑procurement (STEP), and conduct independent audits of grant payments.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement – ASCELC oversight; Fiduciary – anti‑corruption guidelines

gen_risks.description: Insufficient capacity of social workers and field staff may limit effective delivery of economic inclusion services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide comprehensive training, allocate operational budgets for transport and communication, and monitor performance through M&E dashboards.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 3.2 – need for training and operating budget for social workers

gen_risks.description: Remote monitoring tools (GEMS, PDM, IBM) may face data quality issues in insecure or low‑connectivity areas.
gen_risks.mitigation: Combine remote tools with periodic in‑person verification, establish data validation protocols, and train local partners on data entry standards.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 3 – remote monitoring adaptations; Monitoring section – use of GEMS, PDM

gen_risks.description: Delays in rolling out the Unique Social Registry (RSU) to cover all poor households could limit targeting efficiency.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set phased rollout milestones, allocate additional field teams for census sweeps, and monitor coverage percentages monthly.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 2.1 – RSU currently covers ~1/4 of poor households; goal to reach all

gen_risks.description: High turnover or inability to recruit key PIU staff (e.g., gender‑based violence specialist, security specialist) may weaken project governance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer competitive contracts, define clear terms of reference, and maintain a backup pool of qualified consultants.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal Covenants – requirement to recruit GBV and security specialists within 3‑6 months

gen_risks.description: Inadequate grievance redress mechanism performance could lead to unresolved complaints and reputational damage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear SLA for grievance response, train staff on handling SEA/SH cases, and publish quarterly grievance handling statistics.
gen_risks.evidence: ESCP – grievance mechanism to be established within 6 months; Key Risks – grievance handling

gen_risks.description: Funding reductions from donor partners or humanitarian agencies may create resource gaps for IDP support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure multi‑year commitments in the trust fund, build contingency buffers in the budget, and explore private‑sector co‑financing for specific components.
gen_risks.evidence: Strategic Context – recent cuts in humanitarian funding; Funding data shows 0 financing gap but reliance on trust funds

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related supply chain disruptions (e.g., delayed delivery of inputs for IGAs) could affect beneficiary outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Identify alternative local suppliers, pre‑position critical inputs, and incorporate climate risk buffers in procurement timelines.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1.1 – reliance on market‑based inputs; Climate change noted as a shock factor

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk is assessed to be Substantial. The uncertain political and governance context provides a challenge to long-term development policy. Adaptive social protection systems are still nascent and will require continued political commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The team, guided by the management, will continue its high-level policy dialogue at central and decentralized levels and ensure continuous advocacy and communication.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed to be Substantial. Fiscal space remains constrained by elevated security spending and tighter financing conditions, which increase the risk of reduced budget allocations and delayed counterpart funding for new priorities and reforms, including social protection and the PAMPV. Macroeconomic risks also arise from exogenous factors, including current conflict in the Middle East which can result in a surge in oil prices and put inflationary pressure.
gt_risks.mitigation: Other programs such as the International Monetary Fund program and the World Bank's technical assistance on tax expenditure under the Sustainable Development Finance Policy can help expand fiscal space, partially mitigating these risks.

gt_risks.description: Sector strategy and policies risks are considered to be Substantial. Sectoral strategies and policies remain nascent, and the Government's budget allocation to operationalize the PAMPV remains unclear. Also, sectoral decisions are at times taken abruptly and can heavily affect implementation (for example, the suspension of cash transfers in 2023 led to an increased focus on economic inclusion, and the newly emerged priority of the CONASUR/IDPs led to the revision of the fiche de projet of this project).
gt_risks.mitigation: In parallel with high-level policy dialogue, the project supports strategic communications, adopts an agile approach, and provides technical assistance to promote evidence-based decision-making (with support from SASPP, the Social Protection Response MDTF, and the State and Peacebuilding Fund).

gt_risks.description: Overall fiduciary risks are considered as Substantial, as described in section IV.B and annex 2, based on financial assessment and procurement assessment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project preparation fund (Grant Facility for Project Preparation) has been used not only to prepare mitigation measures to address these risks but will also elevate the project readiness (for example, effectiveness-linked actions including FM and procurement staffing and initiating the procurement packages for the first 18-months' implementation priorities) to improve the project performance.

gt_risks.description: Other risks related to insecurity are rated as High. The deteriorating and volatile security situation—particularly in regions with high poverty, displacement, and food insecurity that are project intervention areas—will likely be an important risk. The project will also address other risks related to protection of personal data: for Component 2 on social registry and interoperability, activities will be guided by the Information System Security Policy (ISSP) document developed by the ANSSI, to ensure confidentiality of households registered in the RSU.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project activities will be adjusted based on the security situation (see annex 3), and the PIU will be also staffed with a security specialist and a security management plan will be developed. To remain engaged, the project will also rely on remote delivery/monitoring, partnering with local representation (NGOs, UN agencies). The ST-RSU will conduct capacity-building activities, including training sessions and awareness campaigns, to strengthen users' ability to manage and protect households' personal data.
